items.title: रामलीला मैदान में विपक्ष की रैली: क्या सिर्फ ‘वोट चोरी’ था लोगों का मुद्दा?
items.summary: दिल्ली के रामलीला मैदान में रविवार को इंडिया गठबंधन ने ‘वोट बचाओ, देश बचाओ’ रैली आयोजित की. विपक्षी दलों के नेताओं की इस रैली का मकसद चुनावी सूचियों के विशेष गहन पुनरीक्षण (एसआईआर) के खिलाफ गठबंधन के विरोध को आगे बढ़ाना था. गठबंधन ने पहले मिंटो ब्रिज से रामलीला मैदान तक मार्च निकालने का ऐलान किया था. हालांकि, राहुल गांधी दोपहर करीब 2:30 बजे अखिलेश यादव और तेजस्वी यादव के साथ एक गाड़ी में सवार होकर सीधे रैली स्थल पहुंचे. वहां उन्होंने विशाल जनसभा को संबोधित किया. उनके अलावा मल्लिकार्जुन खड़गे, ममता बनर्जी, फारूक अब्दुल्ला और महबूबा मुफ्ती ने भी सभा को संबोधित किया. रैली में शामिल नेताओं और लोगों ने मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त ज्ञानेश कुमार के इस्तीफे और एसआईआर की प्रक्रिया वापस लेने की मांग की. बिहार, महाराष्ट्र और राजस्थान से आए लोगों ने बताया कि जरूरी दस्तावेज होने के बावजूद मतदाताओं के नाम वोटर लिस्ट से काटे जा रहे हैं. वहीं, कुछ लोगों ने महंगाई, प्रदूषण और महिलाओं की सुरक्षा जैसे मुद्दे भी उठाए. इससे साफ था कि रैली का दायरा केवल ‘वोट चोरी’ के आरोपों तक सीमित नहीं था. न्यूज़लॉन्ड्री ने इस रैली में कई राज्यों से आए राजनीतिक दलों के कार्यकर्ताओं के साथ-साथ ऐसे आम लोगों से भी बात की, जिनका किसी राजनीतिक दल से कोई जुड़ाव नहीं है. हमारे अनुमान के मुताबिक, रैली में कम से कम एक लाख लोग शामिल हुए. मैदान के बाहर भी बड़ी संख्या में लोग मौजूद थे, जिन्हें अंदर जगह नहीं मिल सकी. देखिए पूरा वीडियो दिल्ली के रामलीला मैदान में इंडिया गठबंधन की लोकतंत्र बचाओ रैली कितनी असरदार? भाजपा की रामलीला: सनातन विरोधियों का पुतला दहन और जी20 का जश्न

items.title: Uttarakhand SIR: 2,700+ names deleted in Gadarpur on objections filed by poll officers after the deadline
items.summary: “No eligible voter should be left out” has become the Election Commission’s refrain during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, repeated by Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and in the Election Commission of India (ECI)’s press releases. In Uttarakhand’s Gadarpur constituency, the final roll tells a different story. According to Form 10 records published by the Uttarakhand Chief Electoral Officer (CEO), 10 Assistant Electoral Registration Officers (AEROs) and the Electoral Registration Officer (ERO) filed 2,742 objections to delete voters on just two dates – September 18 (763) and September 28 (1,979). Both dates fell more than a month after the claims and objections period ended on August 13, with the second batch just logged five days before the final electoral roll was published. Rule 17 of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, requires objections lodged after the prescribed period to be rejected. Electoral rules contain no provision for EROs or AEROs to file Form 7 themselves. Yet, according to this report in The Hindu , poll officials in Delhi, West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand have used the route to remove voters flagged for unresolved logical discrepancies or as “unmapped.” Gadarpur ERO Amrita Sharma has maintained that the post-deadline filings were merely procedural delays in generating the forms on the system, and insisted that hearings on the ground had already taken place. Yet Newslaundry met at least 15 deleted voters across Gadarpur who found out their names had been struck off only after the final roll was published. Some said they received initial notices and others said they received none, but all said they were not accorded due process before their names were struck off. They also said poll officials then told them to file a fresh Form 6. ‘There was a slight delay, but I would not call it a mistake’ Asked about the objections filed after the August 13 deadline, Sharma said: “Actually, our officers were not aware that Form 7 also had to be generated for those who were absent. items.title: ‘Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao’: The INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan, as it unfolded
items.summary: The INDIA bloc held its “Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao” rally at Ramlila Maidan in Delhi on Sunday. The rally, attended by leaders from across the Opposition, was part of the bloc’s push against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. They had announced that they would walk from Minto Bridge to Ramlila Maidan, but Rahul Gandhi arrived at the venue around 2.30 pm in a vehicle with Akhilesh Yadav and Tejashwi Yadav. At the venue, they addressed the large gathering, as did Mallikarjun Kharge, Mamata Banerjee, Farooq Abdullah, and Mehbooba Mufti. Leaders and attendees demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and a rollback of the SIR. Attendees from Bihar, Maharashtra and Rajasthan described voters being left off the rolls despite having documents. Others raised inflation, pollution and women’s safety, showing that the rally was not limited to “vote chori”. Newslaundry spoke to party workers from several states and to ordinary citizens with no party affiliations. items.title: Invisible and unprotected: India’s new labour codes fail domestic, home-based workers
items.summary: On a blistering afternoon in June, when the temperature had crossed 40 degrees Celsius, 48-year-old Manju (name changed on request) was at home in the dense Mewla Maharajpur locality. She wanted a few minutes of rest before heading out to work as a domestic worker. But the ceiling fan in the room, recirculating hot air, was not helping her cool down. Dreading the blazing sun, Manju reminded herself that it was only a 20-minute-walk to her employer’s home, and that she had been doing this for decades. A few minutes into the walk, she knew something was terribly wrong. “I began to feel overwhelming thirst, followed by a parched throat and nausea. I sat on the side of the road and managed to get drinking water from someone nearby,” she said. Manju’s symptoms indicate that she may have experienced heat exhaustion that arises due to the body's response to an excessive loss of water and salt, usually through profuse sweating. Yet, she did not return home. “I felt guilty about not showing up for work,” said Manju. India’s four new labour codes, which replaced 29 Union government labour laws, have a blindspot when it comes to protecting workers from the impacts of climate change, as we reported in the first part of our series. The other four parts of this series investigated how women in the manufacturing sector , street vendors, small-site construction workers and gig workers , fall through the labour code protections, leaving them vulnerable to impacts of climate change. Extreme climate has particular impacts on women workers, who juggle work with caregiving responsibilities at home, as we reported in the first part of our series. Safe working conditions, provisions such as paid sick leave, health insurance, maternity benefits, income support during climate disasters, access to cooling infrastructure, and bargaining power, can help shield women workers from climate risks. items.title: Azam Khan moves Supreme Court against arrest by ED after release from jail
items.summary: Samajwadi Party (SP) leader Mohd Azam Khan has approached the Supreme Court challenging his arrest by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) immediately after he was release from jail in another case. The matter was mentioned before Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant before advocate Nizam Pasha. The CJI agreed to hear the case this week. Chief Justice of India Surya Kant Khan and his son Abdullah Azam were granted bail by the Allahabad High Court in the dual PAN card case on October 29. The High Court suspended Khan's 10-year sentence in the dual PAN card case but refused to stay his conviction. Khan and his son were released from Rampur jail on October 31 but Khan was detained by the ED team waiting outside the jail. The ED action came in relation to a separate money laundering case involving alleged financial irregularities concerning Mohammad Ali Jauhar University. A special Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) court in Ghaziabad remanded Khan to 14-day judicial custody on Sunday, November 1. The ED case concerns allegations that agricultural land belonging to farmers were forcibly occupied for Mohammad Ali Jauhar University. The ED initiated money laundering charges against Khan and others based on around 26 first information reports (FIRs) registered by the Uttar Pradesh Police in 2019. items.title: Allahabad High Court directs State to pay ₹1.25 lakh to man for 5-day illegal detention
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court recently ordered the State to pay a compensation of ₹1.25 lakh to a man who was unlawfully detained for five days at a police station [ Gyanti Devi And 2 Others v State of UP & 3 Others ]. A bench of Justice Atul Sreedharan and Justice Achal Sachdev observed that the investigating officer, who had detained the man, demonstrated an "arrogance of authority" by not following the procedure established by law. "The manner in which the I.O. has demonstrated his arrogance of authority, by detaining petitioner No.2 for full five days without even thinking twice and without following the procedure established by law, makes it appear that he considered it business as usual," the Court said. It added that the harshest punishment should be imposed upon the errant errant police officer in case he is found guilty in a departmental inquiry initiated by the police department in the matter. The Court proceeded to order the payment of ₹1.25 lakh to the person who was detained illegally for five days. "This Court is of the opinion that, for the period of five days undergone by petitioner No.2 in custody without adherence to the procedure established by law, compensation at the rate of Rs.25,000/- per day is granted, which amounts to Rs.1,25,000/-. This shall not preclude the right of petitioner No.2 to sue the Police Department in an action in tort for damages," the Court directed. The Court further said that the compensation paid should be recovered from the police officers found guilty of having carried out the illegal detention. "The compensation granted to the petitioner shall be recovered from such persons who, after an inquiry, are found guilty of having detained him. The State may effect such recovery, if so desired," it said. Justice Atul Sreedharan and Justice Achal Sachdev The Court passed the order on a habeas corpus petition moved by one Gyanti Devi who said her son Chandan Rajbhar was detained by the police after he eloped with an 18-year-old woman. An FIR registered in Deoria under Section 87 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita alleged that the woman was kidnapped with the intention of compelling her to enter into a marriage. Rajbhar was taken into custody by Salempur police in district Deoria on August 28. He remained under illegal detention before he was formally arrested on September 2. In response to the plea, the State conceded that the investigating officer Deep Narayan Yadav had illegally detained Rajbhar for five days. Superintendent

items.title: Indian scientist secures patent for in-vivo power generator after Bombay High Court order against IIT
items.summary: The Indian Patent Office has formally approved a patent for scientist Dr. Tarkeshwar Chandrakant Patil, securing his exclusive ownership over an invention capable of generating electrical power inside the human body. This outcome follows a September 8 order of the Bombay High Court in Patil’s decade-long dispute with the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Bombay. The dispute involved an apparatus and a method for in-vivo power generation, a technology designed to keep medical implants active inside the human body. Patil’s patented device functions by converting glucose found in cerebrospinal fluid into a hydrogen-rich fuel, such as ethanol or methanol, using bioenzymes. This fuel powers a nano-scale biofuel cell implanted in the body, creating a self-sustaining power source that mitigates the need for repeated surgeries to replace traditional lithium-ion button batteries. IIT Bombay initially filed the patent application in August 2013. However, after internal disputes, the institute executed a worldwide assignment deed in 2017 transferring all intellectual property rights to Patil. Despite the transfer, IIT-B contested his rights in India, leading to a prolonged delay in him getting the patent. The High Court recently criticised it as a systematic frustration of a premier scientist. Thus, in its order of September 8, the High Court declared Dr. Patil as the original inventor of the patent and directed a Deputy Controller of Patents and Designs to recognize him as the applicant in a patent application filed by IIT Bombay (IITB) in 2013. On October 30, the Assistant Controller of Patents & Designs Aditya Venkateswara NC executed the Court's mandate by substituting Patil as the sole applicant and inventor and set aside the July 2025 rejection. The Controller also dismissed pending technical objections regarding the invention's inventive step.

items.title: Courts reviewing arbitral award on merits defeats purposes of arbitration: Chief Justice Vibhu Bahkru
items.summary: Karnataka High Court Chief Justice Vibhu Bakhru on Saturday said that allowing courts to undertake a full merit-based review of arbitral awards would defeat the fundamental purpose of arbitration, which was intended to provide parties with a final adjudication of disputes outside the traditional court system. Speaking at a conference on Ethics and Evidence in Arbitration in Bengaluru, Justice Bakhru acknowledged concerns over the quality of arbitral awards but cautioned against expanding judicial scrutiny. " But if you have a full merits review then automatically the private arbitration is over ," Justice Bakhru said. The conference was jointly hosted by the London Court of International Arbitration (LCIA), ArbitralWomen and the Arbitration and Conciliation Centre Bengaluru at the Karnataka Judicial Academy. Justice Bakhru made the observation during a fireside conversation with Senior Advocate Shashank Garg , a Court Member of the LCIA, on the hits and misses of India's arbitration landscape. Garg referred to a debate over whether challenges to arbitral awards under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act should permit a more extensive examination of disputes on their merits. Section 34 provides limited grounds for setting aside arbitral awards, including violations of public policy, patent illegality in domestic awards and procedural irregularities. It does not ordinarily permit courts to reconsider disputes as appellate courts would. Justice Bakhru said that demands for broader judicial scrutiny stemmed from dissatisfaction with the quality of some awards. " The quality of awards is not coming up to the standard that you can sit back and say, no, let us review. It is a vicious circle ," he observed. He explained that limited judicial interference depended on arbitrators delivering well-reasoned awards that inspired confidence. When arbitrators delivered high-quality awards, courts could adopt a hands-off approach and refrain from interfering with them, he observed. However, he emphasised that arbitration was founded on the understanding that arbitrators chosen by parties would finally adjudicate their disputes. " It is the arbitrators that people the parties choose are the final adjudicators of the dispute ," he said. items.title: Bhushan Power: NCLT rejects promoters’ challenge to maintainability of government's recovery plea
items.summary: The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) rejected the challenge raised by Bhushan Power and Steel Limited’s (BPSL) former promoters and others to the maintainability of the petition filed by Central government seeking recovery of ₹5,431 crore allegedly diverted from the company. [Union of India Vs BPSL] President Justice Anupinder Singh Grewal and Technical Member Ravindra Chaturvedi held that insolvency resolution and replacement of management did not bar proceedings against those allegedly retaining diverted funds. “ The replacement of the erstwhile management may have brought its control over the company to an end, but it does not, by itself, undo the alleged diversion or remove the prejudice that may have been caused to the company and the public interest, ” the Bench said. The October 30 order dismissed eight applications challenging the maintainability of the government's plea. The applicants included former promoters Sanjay Singal and Aarti Singal, their daughter Priyanka Miglani, associated companies and other individuals. The tribunal confined its decision to whether the petition could be entertained. “ We reiterate that no finding has been recorded on the merits of the allegations, which remain to be adjudicated, ” it clarified. The Union government, through the Serious Fraud Investigation Office (SFIO), filed the petition under Sections 241(2), 242 and 246 read with Section 339 of the Companies Act, 2013. Relying on an SFIO investigation report dated May 6, 2022, it sought to hold the respondents personally liable for at least ₹5,431 crore, besides interest. It also sought attachment and realisation of their assets. The SFIO alleged that funds were siphoned off from BPSL through entities controlled by its former promoters. The transactions allegedly involved routing funds to maintain the debt-equity ratio required for bank financing and purchasing movable and immovable properties. BPSL entered insolvency proceedings in July 2017 and was acquired by JSW Steel in March 2021. The applicants argued that Section 241(2), which addresses affairs that are being conducted prejudicially to public interest, could not cover historical transactions after the former management has been replaced. items.title: Arbitrary power thrives on ignorance, fear: Supreme Court Justice Ujjal Bhuyan
items.summary: Supreme Court Justice Ujjal Bhuyan on Saturday said that scientific temper lays the foundation for the rule of law, since arbitrary power feeds on a society that does not question. A society that stops asking questions becomes vulnerable to authoritarianism, he emphasised. "I believe, scientific temperament lays the foundation for the rule of law. This is because arbitrary power thrives on ignorance, fear and unexamined belief," he said. Thus, a society which believes tradition should be immune from scrutiny will fail to reform unjust practices, he opined. "A society that accepts claims without evidence is susceptible to superstitious beliefs and becomes vulnerable to mis-information. A society that fears questions becomes vulnerable to authoritarianism. A society that treats tradition as beyond scrutiny may fail to reform unjust practices," he said. Justice Bhuyan was delivering the address at the 12th convocation ceremony of the University of Science and Technology Meghalaya (USTM). items.title: India not yet a preferred arbitration seat, cultural shift needed across judiciary and Bar: Justice Manish Pitale
items.summary: Bombay High Court judge Justice Manish Pitale stated that India is currently not featuring as a preferred seat for international commercial arbitration and judiciary, legislature, and the legal profession must work in tandem to drive institutional change. The judge delivered the special address at the ICC India Arbitration Conference in Mumbai. ICC india Arbitration Conference 2026 Justice Pitale noted that international disputants evaluate whether a jurisdiction's domestic legal framework aligns with global standards before selecting an arbitral seat. “India, at the present moment, is obviously not featuring there as one of the preferred seats. What's the reason for this? Where are we going? It's something we need to think about,” he said. The judge highlighted the paradox of Indian businesses choosing foreign venues for dispute resolution. “I came across one (section) 34 challenge in my court where both parties were Indians but the seat of arbitration was Singapore so we have to think why this is happening,” he observed Justice Pitale pointed out that hearing challenges to arbitral awards under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act requires specialized judicial experience rather than an appellate civil court mindset. “The tendency of subconscious thinking of a judge perhaps is like that of an appellate court. It should not be. So this cultural change has to happen, for which you have to have judges who are specialized, who have had exposure to arbitration,” he explained. Justice Pitale remarked that the domestic legal bar must also transition towards institutionalisation and specialized full-time practice. He emphasized that arbitration cannot remain a casual pursuit, noting that a dedicated arbitration bar is essential for professional assistance. “The whole purpose of arbitration is to do resolution and if it leads to bringing people back to square one how is it a solution?” he observed. Justice Pitale concluded that voluntary adherence to basic minimum ethics like impartiality, independence, and timely disclosure will help resolve friction between domestic public policy and global practice. This may enable India to emerge as an international arbitration hub. The conference also featured three technical panel sessions addressing key areas of arbitration practice. items.title: Zoho’s Sridhar Vembu participates in RSS centenary march in Tamil Nadu
items.summary: Zoho co-founder and Chief Scientist Sridhar Vembu participated in a Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) route march in Sankarankovil in Tamil Nadu’s Tenkasi district on November 1 alongside local BJP functionaries. The march was part of the second phase of RSS processions held across several districts to mark the organisation’s centenary year. Ananthan Ayyasamy, a BJP functionary from Tenkasi, shared photographs of the march on X and said Vembu had participated alongside the party’s district and town office-bearers. The November 1 procession was among RSS route marches held across Tamil Nadu following a Madras High Court order allowing the organisation to conduct them on October 25 and November 1, subject to conditions and local police requirements. The High Court on October 16 disposed of a petition after the state government told it that permission would be granted for the marches. Justice V Lakshminarayanan also directed the police to consider future applications in accordance with guidelines laid down in earlier cases and not delay decisions on them. The RSS had approached the court after police denied permission for route marches in the state. The organisation’s state secretary for north Tamil Nadu, V G Jagadeesan, had said it had faced such restrictions since 2022. Vembu’s participation comes months after he spoke about being influenced by a Marxist teacher during his school years. In a post on X in July, he said the teacher’s lessons had turned him into a Marxist and atheist when he was 14, despite his studying at a school funded by an RSS-affiliated individual. He described the experience as being “brainwash[ed]” by the teacher. The second phase of processions on November 1 were held in districts including Tenkasi, Coimbatore, Tiruchirappalli, Madurai, Perambalur, Theni, Dindigul, Tiruppur, Sivaganga and Kanyakumari. items.title: Andhra urban local body polls: Re-polling in 13 stations after booth capture
items.summary: Re-polling is being held in 13 polling stations of seven different urban local bodies in Andhra Pradesh on November 2. The urban local body polls held on November 1 saw many allegations of vote rigging and booth capture allegedly by supporters of the Telugu Desam Party-led coalition government. Four polling stations in Pulivendula municipality were ordered to go for fresh polls as booth capture had taken place, an order from the State Election Commission said on November 1. The counting of votes will happen on November 3. Former chief minister and YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) chief YS Jagan Mohan Reddy had alleged rampant rigging in his constituency Pulivendula and demanded re-polling when he arrived there to cast his vote. His aunt, YS Prameelamma, is the party’s candidate for the post of Pulivendula municipality chairperson. Fresh polls are also being held in one polling station each in Anantapur, Kadapa, and Tirupati municipal corporations, and various polling stations in Macherla, Jammalamadugu, and Chimakurthy municipalities, with the SEC concluding that booth capture had taken place. Final polling figures shared by the SEC showed a 60.96% turnout across the state. Jagan had alleged on November 1 that people who arrived to cast their votes were blocked at polling stations and sent back, women voters threatened, and their voter slips forcibly snatched away before they were sent back. A similar situation prevailed in Kadapa, Jammalamadugu, Chittoor, Macherla, Chilakaluripet, Tadipatri, Madanapalle, and Chimakurthi, Jagan alleged. He slammed Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu for the way elections were being conducted. “If elections are conducted in Andhra Pradesh in this manner, driven by vendetta and deep-seated animosity, what will happen when another party eventually comes to power? Their party workers might ask, If it wasn't wrong when you did it, why should it be wrong when we do it?,” he said.

items.title: Phone used in Siddaramaiah sting row videos handed over at Kumaraswamy’s residence: Police
items.summary: The mobile phone allegedly used to upload videos targeting former Karnataka chief minister Siddaramaiah was handed over to an associate at Union Minister HD Kumaraswamy’s official residence in New Delhi, Bengaluru Police Commissioner Seemant Kumar Singh said on Sunday, November 1. The claim is based on the statement of an accused, and police said they are still verifying the details. The Commissioner said Ritesh Pandey, who was arrested in Delhi on October 24, told investigators that he and Vinod Sharma bought the phone from a shop in Karol Bagh on the instructions of Prajwal Prasad. The two allegedly took the device to Kumaraswamy’s residence on Kushak Road and handed it over to Prajwal, who was present there. “Arrested suspect Ritesh Pandey revealed that he and another person, Vinod Sharma, acted on the instructions of one Prajwal Prasad. This is as per Pandey’s statement. Both Prasad and Sharma are absconding and have moved anticipatory bail petitions,” Seemant said. The commissioner said investigators were examining technical evidence, including CCTV footage and digital records, as well as financial transactions between Ritesh and Prajwal. Police have issued notices to Vinod and Prajwal, but neither has appeared for questioning. Seemant said further interrogation would be important to establish their roles and verify the sequence of events. The case relates to a purported sting video, reportedly filmed in 2023 and recently aired by local television channels, linking Siddaramaiah to allegations of blackmail and a supposed honey-trap network. The case has drawn political attention after Siddaramaiah alleged that the purported sting operation was intended to blackmail him and damage his reputation. On October 29, the commissioner’s office said evidence gathered so far did not substantiate the alleged sexual abuse depicted in the video and described the narrative as “fabricated and deliberately constructed”. A Bengaluru civil court granted an interim injunction restraining certain media organisations and digital platforms from broadcasting or publishing allegedly defamatory content and viral videos linking him to the sting operation. The videos, which surfaced online in September and October, purportedly concerned an incident in 2011 but were allegedly recorded in 2023. items.summary: The Special Investigation Team (SIT) probing the sexual assault cases against Gem Granites owner Veeramani has initiated steps to cancel the passport of businessman Prakash Kanniah, who is suspected of helping Veeramani conceal the alleged offences against minor girls. According to the police, Prakash, who served as an adviser to the Gem group of companies, was allegedly involved in helping the accused evade police action and was also suspected of having a role in the financial transactions connected to the cases. Police suspect that he is currently in the United Kingdom. Police have approached the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) to revoke his passport and take steps to secure him in India. Earlier, a Look Out Circular (LOC) had been issued against him after he failed to appear for questioning. The LOCs are intended to alert authorities at airports, seaports and land borders about individuals sought by investigating agencies. As part of the investigation, the SIT conducted searches at Prakash's office and residential premises. His bank accounts, which had a balance of about Rs 40 crore are now frozen. Investigators have obtained details of his financial transactions over the past three years, particularly between him and companies owned by Veeramani. items.title: Police shoot Andhra chainsaw attacker, say he stabbed inspector
items.summary: Police in Andhra Pradesh shot at and arrested Hemanth, the 21-year-old who attacked two Class 10 students, Gopika and Lakshmi, with a chainsaw inside a classroom in Anantapur district, on Sunday, November 1. Anantapur Superintendent of Police P Jagadeesh said six rounds were fired after Hemanth allegedly attacked police personnel attempting to arrest him near the Atmakur forest area. The accused, Hemanth, entered a classroom at a government school in Raptadu on Saturday, October 31, and attacked a 15-year-old student with a running chainsaw. He also injured another girl who tried to protect her classmate before fleeing the school. Speaking to reporters, Jagadeesh said police teams had been searching for Hemanth since the attack. Acting on information received on Sunday evening, two teams went to the Atmakur forest area, where they found him around 6.30 pm. According to the SP, Hemanth was intoxicated and resisted arrest. Police initially fired warning shots into the air and asked him to surrender, but he allegedly continued to resist and attacked the personnel with a knife, injuring a circle inspector. “Left with no other option, the police teams acted in self defence and fired six rounds at Hemanth and wounded him,” Jagadeesh said. The accused sustained multiple bullet injuries and was taken under police guard to Anantapur Government General Hospital at around 8.30 pm for emergency treatment. Jagadeesh said his condition was critical, with multiple wounds below the waist. The SP also said Hemanth appeared to have sustained an injury to his face before the encounter. One of the injured students, Gopika, suffered extensive injuries, including the severing of her right hand, fractures and damage to blood vessels. She was initially treated at Anantapur Government General Hospital before being transferred to Manipal Hospital in Bengaluru through a green corridor for advanced treatment. The second student Lakshmi was injured while attempting to intervene in the attack. Doctors in Anantapur administered 10 units of blood to the critically injured girl before she was shifted to Bengaluru. She underwent surgery at Manipal Hospital and was moved to the intensive care unit. Andhra Pradesh Education Minister Nara Lokesh visited her in Bengaluru on Sunday and said the next 48 hours would be crucial.
